subject: CloudBridge price match request + migration compatibility questions
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudbridge.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@cloudbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Price match request + compatibility questions

Diego —

Appreciate the earlier demo. Short version: our procurement team received a renewal offer from Voltix that is materially lower on token price and includes a migration credit. Before we proceed with a full competitive process, we wanted to give Redwood a chance to match economically and to confirm technical compatibility for our inference workload.

Two asks:
1) Can you provide a price-match proposal that covers 12 months (token-based) and a migration credit? Voltix is offering a blended token discount that equates to ~28% off list for our expected volume.
2) Can you confirm runtime compatibility for our latency-sensitive LL-based inference (avg request size 350 tokens, 95th latency SLO 250ms), including whether your quantized variants behave equivalently for our LLM stack (we use a 7B encoder-decoder).

I attached our baseline usage and current spend for context (CloudBridge_Baseline_Usage.pdf). Procurement would like an initial response by EOD tomorrow if possible.

If useful, happy to hop on a short call — Sarah and I are available 10:30–12 PT.

Thanks,
Ethan

--
Ethan Cole
Director, Platform Engineering
CloudBridge, Inc.
ethan.cole@cloudbridge.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Price match request + compatibility questions

Ethan —

Thanks for the context and the attachment; appreciated. We can absolutely respond quickly. High-level: we typically consider a blended concession (credits + token discount) tied to a 12-month commit and an operational handoff that minimizes migration risk. That said, the two technical points you call out are what really determine whether we can match Voltix without incurring operational risk.

To give you a meaningful price-match we need two small clarifications:
- Can you share a 48-hour trace (or representative 1k requests) showing latency distribution and average prompt/response sizes?
- Is the model family fully open (weights + tokenizer) or a containerized proprietary runtime? Quantization/variant availability differs across those cases.

Action plan:
- If you can share the trace, we’ll run a perf-pass and produce a short migration-risk note (runtime fit, quantization plan, warm-start expectations) plus an econ sheet with a proposed blended match.
- I’m attaching a quick checklist we use for takeovers (redwood_takeover_checklist.docx).

We can take a 20–30 minute call today at 11:00 PT to align on the trace and timing if that works.

Best,
Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: CloudBridge price match request — suggested concession + technical guardrails

Diego / Marcus / Marissa —

Quick internal notes after reading Ethan’s ask and Diego’s response:
- Commercial suggestion: offer a 12-month blended proposal that combines a 20% token discount off list + a migration credit calculated as 3 months of expected spend (based on the attached baseline). We should structure the credit so it is amortized over Q1 of the renewal so it doesn’t depress ARR recognition in year one.
- Risk/technical guardrails: only offer full parity if our perf report shows their latency distribution maps within our 95th SLO when using our L3 quantized variant. If the L3 quantized variant increases 95th latency >20% for their tail requests we should: (a) push a graduated fallback model (higher-cost variant for tail), and (b) include a 90-day warm-start SLA with reduced credits if warm-start fails.
- Migration incentives: include 1) a dedicated migration engineer for the first 30 days, 2) a runbook and 48-hour rollback window, and 3) a post-migration performance review tied to a small earn-back clause.

Attachments to prepare: CB_migration_econ_v1.xlsx (econ calc), redwood_runbook_v1.pdf (operations), and our takeover checklist (already attached). Marcus — can you run a quick perf-sim with the sample trace once Diego gets it? Marissa — I’ll draft the HubSpot deal note and the proposed concession language for legal.

—Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Operations, Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@cloudbridge.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Price match request + compatibility questions

Ethan —

Thanks again for the baseline doc and for the call earlier. We ran a rapid read of the numbers and drafted an initial offer and runbook based on the assumptions you shared. High-level proposal below; full econ & runbook attached.

Initial commercial offer (conditional on perf pass):
- 12-month commitment with a blended 20% token discount off Redwood list pricing for your expected volume band.
- One-time migration credit equal to estimated 3 months of current spend, paid as a billing credit and amortized over the first invoice cycle.
- Dedicated migration engineer for the first 30 days + a 48-hour rollback window.

Technical commitments & guardrails:
- We will run a perf pass against a 1k-request sample trace you provide. If our L3 quantized variant meets your 95th latency SLO (<=250ms) and functional parity checks, we will qualify the offer as "full parity".
- If the quantized variant fails the tail SLO but passes average latency, we will propose a graduated fallback: route tail requests to a non-quantized (higher-cost) variant automatically with cost/latency thresholds.
- 90-day warm-start period: if we cannot reach parity after the mitigation above, we will provide an earn-back credit (pro-rated) per the attached econ sheet.

Attachments: CB_migration_econ_v1.xlsx (econ + amortization), redwood_runbook_v1.pdf (migration runbook), redwood_takeover_checklist.docx.

Next steps: please send the 1k-request trace (or 48-hour trace) and we’ll schedule Marcus to run the perf-sim within 24 hours. If you want the commercial language in a one-page LOI we can produce that by tomorrow EOD.

Looking forward —
Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
